title: Yash Explains Why He Chose Ravana Over Lord Rama in Ramayana
excerpt: The K.G.F. star says the demon king's inner contradictions and tragic complexity made Ravana an irresistible role in Nitesh Tiwari's two-part epic.
body:
• K.G.F. star Yash has opened up about his decision to play Ravana rather than Rama in Nitesh Tiwari's two-part Ramayana, calling the character's inner contradictions irresistible.
  • Director Tiwari says the film will portray Ravana as a multi-faceted figure — warrior, musician, scholar, and Shiva devotee — rather than a one-dimensional villain.
  • The epic, starring Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama and Sai Pallavi as Sita, is scheduled for a Diwali 2026 release with Part 2 following in Diwali 2027.
  • Yash is also producing the film through his banner Monster Mind Creations, making it a deeply personal project.

The Appeal of Ravana's Complexity

https://youtube.com/watch?v=1zip1rNaNYs

Kannada superstar Yash, best known for the blockbuster K.G.F. franchise, has explained why he chose to portray the demon king Ravana rather than Lord Rama in director Nitesh Tiwari's ambitious two-part cinematic adaptation of the Ramayana — and his answer reveals an actor drawn to complexity over heroism.

"I don't look at anything in black and white," Yash told Collider in an interview at CinemaCon 2026. "When I see Ravana doing so many bad things, that is bad, but I also try to see what are the good qualities he had. Though Ravana is hated so much, there are certain things which people have always appreciated. They've praised the qualities of him."

The actor, who is also producing the film through his banner Monster Mind Creations, described Ravana as a character who "crossed the line" — driven by ego and vengeance to the point where his extraordinary gifts became his undoing.

"Lord Rama is somebody who is born as a king, but goes into situations where he has to lose everything and then regain all his power. But Ravana starts with nothing, becomes powerful and then, sometimes, like they say, when you fight a demon, you end up becoming a bigger one."

— Yash, at Comic-Con 2026

A Ravana Never Seen Before

Director Nitesh Tiwari, speaking to Collider in Los Angeles, revealed that the film's portrayal of Ravana would break significantly from traditional screen depictions. "He had so many aspects to his life," Tiwari said. "He was a great warrior, an accomplished musician, a scholar, a benevolent king, a great Shiva devotee. So there was so much more to him than just being one black character."

https://x.com/bolly_talkies/status/2088831459415183704

Tiwari explained that showcasing Ravana's virtues serves a specific moral purpose in the narrative. "Why it is important for us to showcase all these bits and aspects of his life, is because there is a very important lesson which is hiding in them. You can have all these great qualities, but if you are governed by vengeance and if you are driven by ego, then you know what the end results are going to be."

The film's trailer, unveiled on July 30, opens with Yash's Ravana making a dramatic entrance, declaring himself the new ruler of Lanka. It also showcases the reimagined Pushpaka Vimana — the mythological flying vehicle depicted as a golden lotus with rotating petals — and teases a spectacular action sequence between Ravana and the mythical bird Jatayu, according to the Hollywood Reporter India.

A Personal Connection to the Epic

For Yash, the Ramayana is not merely a professional project but a deeply personal one. "It's probably the first story I ever heard," he told Bollywood Hungama at Comic-Con. "My grandfather used to tell me these stories, and you build your own imagination around them."

The actor admitted the role carries a different kind of pressure compared to his original characters like Rocky in K.G.F. "When you are playing somebody everybody knows, or there have been many versions of it, they will draw comparisons and also have fixed notions about how this character should look, speak, or behave," he said. "It's a mixed feeling — excitement and a little bit of pressure."

Yash said he spent extensive time with Tiwari before shooting began, asking "all possible questions" to understand the director's vision. He described trying to make Ravana "more human" in terms of voice and body language, acknowledging it was a departure from anything he had done before.

A Two-Part Epic for IMAX

Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Sunny Deol in an undisclosed role, and Ravie Dubey. With a reported total runtime of six hours across both parts, the IMAX-formatted production is being positioned as one of the most ambitious Indian films ever made.

Part 1 is scheduled for release during Diwali 2026, with Part 2 following in Diwali 2027. The visual effects are being handled by DNEG, the Oscar-winning studio behind films like Oppenheimer and Dune. Yash teased that the action sequences, particularly the Ravana-Jatayu confrontation, would push the boundaries of what audiences have seen in Indian cinema.

"He's Ravana, he's the best warrior, he's got so many powers. You have to see it to believe it," Yash told media. "The way the scene unfolds — it's magic and full-on commercial action, with the bird in the sky, with the Pushpak Vimana. It is going to be spectacular."
nri_angle: Ramayana is a cultural touchstone for the Indian diaspora worldwide, and the film's global IMAX release is being closely watched by NRI audiences.
